key_insight: Machine learning classified ECT seizure adequacy from raw EEG with ROC AUC above 0.9 for null-response versus threshold and threshold versus adequate seizures.
clinical_relevance: Automated EEG assessment could support more objective ECT dosing decisions, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Assigned expert labels: null-response, threshold, or adequate.
Trained and evaluated multiple machine learning classifiers using raw EEG.
evidence_signal: The best model achieved ROC AUC above 0.9 for both reported category comparisons; adding clinical variables did not improve performance.
watch_item: This proof-of-concept study showed only moderate prediction of seizure quality in subsequent treatments, limiting claims about prospective dosing support.
paper_title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
